newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen dragged down by Dow.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen dragged down by Dow.

text.p: Argentine stocks were expected to post heavy losses at the opening Friday on the back of a selloff in New York stocks and bonds, dealers said.

"The market will react to the U.S. payrolls data, which was unfavorable and caused the long bond yield to swing back up to 6.4 percent (from Thursday's 6.3 percent close) in New York," said Miguel Daneri at traders Boston Securities.

However, he did not expect the local market to remain in negative territory for long, "because forecasts for company results due in next week remain good and this fall should be considered an opportunity to buy."
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index closed slightly higher at 850.03 Thursday, stretching gains so far in the week to 1.1 percent.
Early Friday the Dow shed 1.1 percent after the July jobs data showed a surge in payrolls and a drop in unemployment.

"However, average earnings were flat, showing there really are no inflationary pressures, so I don't think a Federal Reserve rate hike is in store," another dealer said. "The markets will use this bad news to consolidate and take some profits, but the trend remains positive."
